clue.text: With the creator of Peter Grimes cutting introduction already composed

indicators.note: cutting introduction says the composer's surname loses its opening letter

parts.note: Benjamin Britten wrote the opera Peter Grimes

explanation.surface: A music critic notes that the Peter Grimes composer edited an overture that was already finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something composed has been set down in words or notes, the past participle of write.

clue.text: Reason for guttering in Ireland?

parts.note: a candle gutters, dripping and flickering, when its wick burns down low; read that way the Irish county's name explains guttering

explanation.surface: Someone asks why the gutters overflow so often on the Irish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guttering' suggests roof drains; here it is what a candle does when it burns down. WICKLOW is a county in Ireland, south of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: The county is in Ireland, and its name split in two describes a candle burning down to its base.

clue.text: Irate mum upset with behaviour of child

indicators.note: upset means the letters of irate mum are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry mother is upset by her child's misbehaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour is the mark of someone not yet grown up, lacking adult judgment.

clue.text: Leader of thieves, one who'll take property of those people

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from thieves

parts.note: an heir is someone who will inherit property

explanation.surface: The chief of a gang of thieves plans to make off with other people's belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to those people already mentioned.

clue.text: Frost in fruits destroying one universal sustenance

indicators.note: in says the frost word sits inside the fruit pair
destroying means a letter is knocked out of the pair of fruits

parts.note: fruits gives two nuts, NUT and NUT
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal, and one says only a single U goes
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that frost on the fruit has ruined one source of food for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying one universal' removes a single U from the pair of fruits, and 'in' puts the frost inside, after the first nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishing food is sustenance: what keeps a living thing going.

clue.text: Second most important part for a musical work

parts.note: the core is the central, essential part of something

explanation.surface: A composer says the second section is the heart of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The written-out music of a composition, especially for a film or show, is its score.

clue.text: What's small and caught by Egyptian, perhaps?

definitions.text: What's small and caught by Egyptian, perhaps?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an Egyptian is an example of an Arab

explanation.surface: A riddle about some tiny creature an Egyptian might catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the sacred beetle of ancient Egypt is small and might be caught by an Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: The dung beetle revered in ancient Egypt is little and found there, so an Egyptian might catch one.

clue.text: Noted actor, one appearing in musical

indicators.note: appearing in says the numeral goes inside the show's title

parts.note: Oliver! is the musical based on Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A famous actor turns up in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was among the most celebrated stage and screen actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: One written of English pasture seen over top of gravestones?

indicators.note: in a down entry the pasture word sits over the letter from the gravestones, on either side of it

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass for grazing

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here from gravestones

explanation.surface: A churchyard picture: English grazing land visible above the headstones.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem is something written, especially one for the dead.

clue.text: Perhaps Brahms or Bach — tips for exams

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the composer

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters, here from exams

explanation.surface: Advice on which composers to revise before the music exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms's first name is an example of the German form of John.

clue.text: Philosopher's place as old college's head, the flower of Cambridge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from college's

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Cam runs through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A philosopher's college post is described as Cambridge's finest bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river (it flows), not a bloom. William of Ockham, of the razor, was named after the Surrey village spelt this way in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The English village is the birthplace of William of Ockham, whose name it gives him.

clue.text: Minor actor takes issue over play's extension

parts.note: an extra is a background performer in a film or play

indicators.note: over means the word for issue is turned round

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: A bit-part player objects to a production running longer.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, extra time is an additional period of play added when a match is level.

clue.text: Very well cast hollow legs built into table

indicators.note: built into says the hollowed legs go inside the table word

parts.note: an altar is a table in a church

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of legs is removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A carpenter's note about legs fitted into a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast full of leading names is one made up entirely of stars.

clue.text: Irrationality shown when hiding son's foolishness

indicators.note: hiding means the son's letter is kept out of sight, removed from the word

parts.note: insanity can mean extreme foolishness
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Some foolish behaviour is shown up when a boy is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Senselessness or lack of sense is irrationality, as in the pointlessness of a remark.

clue.text: Not so very tired and always very urgent

parts.note: no says something is not so
worn, as in worn out, means very tired
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Someone says they are not that exhausted and are always in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a chance that must be seized at once, so a matter that is very urgent.

clue.text: Give decoration to me when returning — like a gong?

indicators.note: returning says the word me is read backwards

parts.note: a gong is bell-like, so bellish

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be decorated on coming home, perhaps with a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' is British slang for a medal, which feeds the surface, but here it is the instrument that sounds like a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to add ornament to it, to give it decoration.

clue.text: Ironic, with good edge

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A remark that is sardonic but with a good cutting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim humour is dark and sardonic, close to the bitter sense of ironic.

clue.text: Almost speechless, turning to croaking, resulting in a loss of clarity

definitions.text: resulting in a loss of clarity

indicators.note: turning says the shortened word is turned round
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
to croak is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone nearly struck dumb begins to croak, and their speech becomes unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' shortens the speechless word by one letter and 'turning' reverses what is left. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring up sediment clouds water, so making things murky means making them less clear.

clue.text: Prince getting hot in rowing boat for a while

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

indicators.note: in says the letter for hot goes inside the boat

parts.note: a four is a racing boat rowed by four oarsmen
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A prince gets hot rowing a boat for some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty minutes is a spell of time, a while.

clue.text: Thicket with singular hedgerow fruit

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn, a hedgerow shrub

explanation.surface: A dense hedge bearing a single berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means a small wood or thicket.

clue.text: Short month, otherwise I worked with deductions

indicators.note: short means the month loses its last letter

parts.note: April is a month
or means otherwise, as in hurry or you'll be late

explanation.surface: Someone worked through a brief month, deductions taken from their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deductions' suggests pay cuts; here it is logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning from first principles to conclusions works by deduction rather than from experience.

clue.text: Brat cadets unfortunately are not concentrating

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of brat cadets end up jumbled

explanation.surface: Unruly military cadets are not paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in thought is absent-minded, not concentrating.

clue.text: Taking progressive positions, The Who found leaden sound synthesizer created sounded like heavy metal

annotationWithheld.why: Taking progressive positions, The Who found leaden sound synthesizer created: the 1st letter of the first word, the 2nd of the second, and so on through seven words. That is seven nth picks under one indicator, and the grammar requires a separate indicator for each one
annotationWithheld.clue: Taking progressive positions, The Who found leaden sound synthesizer created sounded like heavy metal

clue.text: Wounded by what's nearly all let fly

parts.note: hurt means wounded

indicators.note: nearly all means the word let loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone injured by something that was mostly allowed to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by what's' is a link. 'let fly' looks like one phrase; 'fly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush at great speed is to fly, as in hurtling down a hill.

clue.text: Great swimmer taking part in decider or qualifier

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An athlete takes part in a final or a qualifying heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests an athlete; it is a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: A baleen whale such as the blue or fin whale is a huge sea creature, a great swimmer.

clue.text: Nearly all received first among thesauri ——this one?

indicators.note: nearly means the radio word loses its last letter

parts.note: Roger is the radio codeword meaning message received

indicators.note: first among means the first letter of thesauri

explanation.surface: A dictionary user asks which reference book comes top of the thesauri.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mark Roget compiled the best-known English thesaurus, so 'this one' points back to thesauri.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous thesaurus is named after its compiler, so it is one of the thesauri the clue mentions.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory levy is not working

parts.note: off means below standard, as in an off day
a duty is a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A complaint that a poor tax isn't doing its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off duty is not at work, free of their usual responsibilities.

clue.text: No Scottish company flies over the Atlantic?

indicators.note: in a down entry, flying over means the letters go back up, reversed

parts.note: nae is Scots for no

explanation.surface: A Scottish airline does not fly across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the Atlantic as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is one example of a great sea.

clue.text: Spooky, involving sleight, OK?

indicators.note: involving here means rolling or twisting together, so the letters of sleight and ok are churned up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a conjuring trick that seems eerie is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky means eerie, as if haunted by a phantom.

clue.text: Of an earlier age, happy and prosperous — but not the earliest

indicators.note: not the earliest means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a golden age is a happy and prosperous one

explanation.surface: A golden age, happy and prosperous, but not the very first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden days are times long past, an earlier age.

clue.text: Double wicket destroyed as number four is run out

indicators.note: destroyed means the remaining letters of wicket are smashed into a new order
run out, the cricket dismissal, here means the letter is sent out of the word

parts.note: the fourth letter of the word wicket is K

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a double strike destroys the wicket as the fourth batsman is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the fourth letter, K, from WICKET leaves WICET, which is rearranged. A run out is a way a batsman is dismissed in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times over is double, as in twice the amount.

clue.text: Five score in county division

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, so five of them make the number after ninety-nine
an old administrative district of an English shire, with its own court

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. English shires were once split into districts for courts and taxes, each named after that number.
explanation.definitionFit: Five twenties make that number, and it was also the old name for a subdivision of an English shire.
